text.en:
At lunch the playground was full of paper, peels and plastic wrappers.
"Who dropped all this?" asked Riya's teacher.
The class decided to clean up. They used two bins: one for peels and leaves, one for paper and plastic.

Things we throw away are waste.
Wet waste comes from plants and food: peels, leaves, leftover food. It can become compost for plants.
Dry waste is paper, plastic, glass and metal.
We can reduce waste by using less. We can reuse things, like writing on both sides of paper or using a cloth bag. We can recycle: old paper and bottles can be made into new things.
Never throw waste on the road or in water. Use a dustbin.
Waste is what we throw away. Wet waste is food and plant waste, like peels and leaves.
Dry waste is paper, plastic, glass and metal. Keep them in a separate bin.
Reduce: use less. Reuse: use again. Recycle: make something new from old.
Always put waste in a dustbin. A clean place is a happy place.

problem.en: A banana peel, an old newspaper and a plastic bottle: which are wet waste and which are dry?

text.en: The banana peel comes from food. It is wet waste.

why.en: Wet waste comes from food and plants.

text.en: The newspaper and plastic bottle are dry waste.

why.en: Paper and plastic are dry waste.
Separating helps us reuse and recycle.

prompt.en: A friend throws a wrapper on the ground because 'it is only one'. What will you tell your friend?

requiredIdeas.en: Waste should go into a dustbin.
Many small wrappers make a big mess; reduce, reuse and recycle.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking one wrapper does not matter.

points.en: Wet waste is from food and plants; dry waste is paper, plastic, glass and metal.
